LOOK: MMDA workers line up tents that will serve as covered walkways leading to the image of Jesus Nazareno, as thousands of devotees are expected to troop to the Quirino Grandstand in Manila for the “Pahalik,” on Monday, Jan. 5.

The tents are intended to protect pilgrims from the sun and possible rain while ensuring the smooth flow of foot traffic during the religious activity.

📸: Mark Balmores/MB

ANO ANG TRABAHO NI TORRE SA MMDA?

Pangangasiwaan ni Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) General Manager Usec. Nicolas Torre III ang day-to-day operations ng ahensya, ayon kay MMDA Chairman Atty. Don Artes.

Pangungunahan ni Torre ang mga inisyatibang may kinalaman sa public safety, flood control, traffic management, at solid waste management sa National Capital Region.

Magsisilbi rin siyang spokesperson ng ahensya.

"I am excited to join the ranks of the people who keep the metropolis moving [...] where we all live, dream, work and do business in, as my new career in government service. I do hope that I will make the contribution expected of me in MMDA," sabi ni Torre.

LOOK: Students and youth groups staged a protest along Kalaw Avenue near the United States Embassy in Manila on Monday, Jan. 5, to condemn what they described as recent attacks and destabilization efforts against Venezuela, actions they said undermine the country’s sovereignty and endanger the lives and welfare of the Venezuelan people. 

The rally also denounced alleged U.S. imperialist aggression and called for respect for Venezuela’s right to self-determination. 

📸: Mark Balmores/MB
